review_source: Review text supplied by the human principal investigator in ChatGPT after CCS-016 completed
scope_note: The supplied review evaluates the reported CCS-016 results, but the conversation does not establish that Opus 4.6 directly inspected the repository artifacts or independently reran the checker.
review_findings: The reported correctness result was accepted in the review, subject to the scope limitation above.
The 10-versus-12 line-churn difference was judged too small to support a practically meaningful adaptation-burden difference at this scale.
The code-versus-configuration separation was identified as the more interesting observed property: compositional adaptation changed configuration while conventional adaptation changed code.
Any claim that this separation compounds into an advantage at larger scale remains a hypothesis requiring measurement.
CCS-015 and CCS-016 primarily tested deterministic policy logic and did not exercise runtime language interpretation.
The next comparison should test runtime interpretation and should compare a conventional rules system, a simple workflow using the same LLM, and the compositional workflow using that same LLM.

effect_on_record.locality_observation: Compositional lane changed policy configuration without changing engine code; conventional lane changed code. This is an observed modularity/locality property, not yet a demonstrated cost advantage.
